title: epan: reassemble: Only copy fragment data once for partial reassemblies
description:
Normally when a reassembly completes, the tvbuffers for each
fragment_item are discarded (and freed if necessary.) Some protocols,
notably TCP but also including other protocols that present a bytestream
to the next dissector, are sometimes informed by the next dissector
that the reassembly which was thought to be complete is actually not.
This is particularly common when the next protocol does not necessarily
have a length field in its PDU, but continues until a sentinal, or
in some other situations. (HTTP, particularly with chunking, is an
example.)

But since the data has already been copied, this is unnecessary. We can
just indicate with the FD_DEFRAGMENTED flag that the fragment was already
used, and avoid recreating the tvbuffer (as a subset of the previously
completed reassembly) and copying it back into place later.

This is considerably faster on the files contained in #14382.

This also means that the fragment_add_seq functions can use the common
fragment_reset_defragmentation function, since they don't have to
worry about calculating offsets for tvbuffer subsets.

AI-Assisted: no

 extern "C" {
 #endif
 
-/* only in fd_head: packet is defragmented */
+/* in fd_head: packet is defragmented
+ * in item: this item was used in defragmentation
+ * (An item can have this set when the head does not if defragmentation

+ */
 #define FD_DEFRAGMENTED		0x0001
